sanskrit: evaṃ vai sukhaduḥkhābhyāṃ hīnam asti padaṃ kva cit eṣā mama matiḥ sarpa yathā vā manyate bhavān
english: Indeed such a state exists somewhere, free from both pleasure and pain — this is my view, O serpent; or what does your lordship think?

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca yadi te vṛttato rājan brāhmaṇaḥ prasamīkṣitaḥ vyarthā jātis tadāyuṣman kṛtir yāvan na dṛśyate
english: The serpent said: If, O king, you judge a brahmin by his conduct, then birth is meaningless, O long-lived one — so long as virtuous action is not seen.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca jātir atra mahāsarpa manuṣyatve mahāmate saṃkarāt sarvavarṇānāṃ duṣparīkṣyeti me matiḥ
english: Yudhishthira said: Here, O great serpent, O great-minded one, birth in the human world is hard to ascertain, due to the intermixing of all the castes — this is my view.

sanskrit: sarve sarvāsv apatyāni janayanti yadā narāḥ vāṅ maithunam atho janma maraṇaṃ ca samaṃ nṛṇām
english: When all men beget offspring in all women, and speech, sexual union, birth, and death are the same for all human beings —

sanskrit: idam ārṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca ye yajāmaha ity api tasmāc chīlaṃ pradhāneṣṭaṃ vidur ye tattvadarśinaḥ
english: — and this is the ancient authority too, as in the formula 'we who sacrifice' — therefore those who perceive the truth know that good conduct is of supreme importance.

sanskrit: prāṅ nābhivardhanāt puṃso jātakarma vidhīyate tatrāsya mātā sāvitrī pitā tv ācārya ucyate
english: Before the navel-string ceremony, the birth-rite is prescribed for a man; therein his mother is the Savitri and his teacher is said to be his father.

sanskrit: vṛttyā śūdrasamo hy eṣa yāvad vede na jāyate asminn evaṃ matidvaidhe manuḥ svāyambhuvo 'bravīt
english: By occupation he is equal to a shudra until he is born again in the Veda. On this difference of view, Manu the self-born spoke thus:

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyāḥ punar varṇā yadi vṛttaṃ na vidyate saṃkaras tatra nāgendra balavān prasamīkṣitaḥ
english: If the castes, though having performed their duties, do not possess right conduct, then there, O lord of serpents, confusion is seen to be powerful indeed.

sanskrit: yatredānīṃ mahāsarpa saṃskṛtaṃ vṛttam iṣyate taṃ brāhmaṇam ahaṃ pūrvam uktavān bhujagottama
english: Whoever now, O great serpent, possesses refined conduct — him I have previously called a brahmin, O best of serpents.

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca śrutaṃ viditavedyasya tava vākyaṃ yudhiṣṭhira bhakṣayeyam ahaṃ kasmād bhrātaraṃ te vṛkodaram
english: The serpent said: I have heard your words, O Yudhishthira, you who know what is to be known. For what reason then should I eat your brother Vrikodara?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhavān etādṛśo loke vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ brūhi kiṃ kurvataḥ karma bhaved gatir anuttamā
english: Yudhishthira said: You are such a one in this world, versed in the Vedas and Vedangas — tell me, by performing what action does a person reach the highest state?

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca pātre dattvā priyāṇy uktvā satyam uktvā ca bhārata ahiṃsānirataḥ svargaṃ gacched iti matir mama
english: The serpent said: By giving to a worthy recipient, by speaking kind words, by speaking truth, O Bharata, and by being devoted to non-injury — one goes to heaven; this is my view.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dānād vā sarpa satyād vā kim ato guru dṛśyate ahiṃsāpriyayoś caiva gurulāghavam ucyatām
english: Yudhishthira said: Between giving and truth, O serpent, which of these is seen as weightier? And among non-injury and kindly speech, let the relative weight be stated.

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca dāne ratatvaṃ satyaṃ ca ahiṃsā priyam eva ca eṣāṃ kāryagarīyastvād dṛśyate gurulāghavam
english: The serpent said: Devotion to giving, truth, non-injury, and kindly speech — the relative weight of these is determined by the gravity of the action to be performed.

sanskrit: kasmāc cid dānayogād dhi satyam eva viśiṣyate satyavākyāc ca rājendra kiṃ cid dānaṃ viśiṣyate
english: In some circumstances truth surpasses even the practice of giving, O king of kings; and in some cases giving surpasses truthful speech.

sanskrit: evam eva maheṣvāsa priyavākyān mahīpate ahiṃsā dṛśyate gurvī tataś ca priyam iṣyate
english: Similarly, O great archer, O lord of earth, non-injury is seen to be weightier than kindly speech, and then kindly speech is deemed superior.

sanskrit: evam etad bhaved rājan kāryāpekṣam anantaram yad abhipretam anyat te brūhi yāvad bravīmy aham
english: Such is the matter, O king — it depends upon the action at hand. Whatever else you have in mind, ask me while I am speaking to you.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ svarge gatiḥ sarpa karmaṇāṃ ca phalaṃ dhruvam aśarīrasya dṛśyeta viṣayāṃś ca bravīhi me
english: Yudhishthira said: How does one go to heaven, O serpent? And how is the sure fruit of actions seen by one who has no body? Tell me about the objects of sense also.

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca tisro vai gatayo rājan paridṛṣṭāḥ svakarmabhiḥ mānuṣyaṃ svargavāsaś ca tiryagyoniś ca tat tridhā
english: The serpent said: There are indeed three states of existence, O king, determined by one's own actions: humanity, dwelling in heaven, and birth in animal wombs — that is the threefold division.

sanskrit: tatra vai mānuṣāl lokād dānādibhir atandritaḥ ahiṃsārthasamāyuktaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ svargam aśnute
english: From the human world, one who is diligent through giving and the like, combined with causes relating to non-injury and truthfulness, attains heaven.

sanskrit: viparītaiś ca rājendra kāraṇair mānuṣo bhavet tiryagyonis tathā tāta viśeṣaś cātra vakṣyate
english: By contrary causes, O king of kings, one becomes human again; or takes birth in animal wombs, dear one — the distinction in this regard will be stated.

sanskrit: kāmakrodhasamāyukto hiṃsālobhasamanvitaḥ manuṣyatvāt paribhraṣṭas tiryagyonau prasūyate
english: One who is possessed of desire and anger, who is accompanied by violence and greed, falls from humanity and is born in an animal womb.

sanskrit: tiryagyonyāṃ pṛthagbhāvo manuṣyatve vidhīyate gavādibhyas tathāśvebhyo devatvam api dṛśyate
english: Separate gradations exist even within animal births; in humanity gradations are established; and from among cattle, horses, and the like, even divinity is seen to be attainable.

sanskrit: so 'yam etā gatīḥ sarvā jantuś carati kāryavān nitye mahati cātmānam avasthāpayate nṛpa
english: Thus this being, acting purposefully, traverses all these states, and finally establishes itself in the great eternal, O king.

sanskrit: jāto jātaś ca balavān bhuṅkte cātmā sa dehavān phalārthas tāta niṣpṛktaḥ prajālakṣaṇabhāvanaḥ
english: Born again and again, powerful, the embodied self enjoys; its purpose is fruit, dear one — it remains unattached, experiencing the characteristics of creation.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śabde sparśe ca rūpe ca tathaiva rasagandhayoḥ tasyādhiṣṭhānam avyagraṃ brūhi sarpa yathātatham
english: Yudhishthira said: In sound, touch, form, and similarly in taste and smell — tell me clearly the undistracted basis of that self, O serpent, exactly as it is.

sanskrit: kiṃ na gṛhṇāsi viṣayān yugapat tvaṃ mahāmate etāvad ucyatāṃ coktaṃ sarvaṃ pannagasattama
english: Why do you not apprehend the objects of sense simultaneously, O great-minded one? Let this much be explained — and also all that has been said, O best of serpents.

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca yad ātmadravyam āyuṣman dehasaṃśrayaṇānvitam karaṇādhiṣṭhitaṃ bhogān upabhuṅkte yathāvidhi
english: The serpent said: That which is the substance of the self, O long-lived one, connected with the body's dwelling, presided over by the organs of sense — it enjoys objects of experience in due order.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ caivātra buddhiś ca manaś ca bharatarṣabha tasya bhogādhikaraṇe karaṇāni nibodha me
english: Cognition, intellect, and mind, O bull of the Bharatas — learn from me about these as the instruments in the experiencing of that self.

sanskrit: manasā tāta paryeti kramaśo viṣayān imān viṣayāyatanasthena bhūtātmā kṣetraniḥsṛtaḥ
english: Through the mind, dear one, the elemental self — situated at the abode of the sense objects, gone forth from the field — goes to these sense objects one by one in sequence.

sanskrit: atra cāpi naravyāghra mano jantor vidhīyate tasmād yugapad asyātra grahaṇaṃ nopapadyate
english: Here too, O tiger among men, the mind of a being is determined to be singular; therefore simultaneous apprehension of all objects at once is not possible for it.

sanskrit: sa ātmā puruṣavyāghra bhruvor antaram āśritaḥ dravyeṣu sṛjate buddhiṃ vividheṣu parāvarām
english: That self, O tiger among men, residing between the eyebrows, produces intellect — higher and lower — in relation to various objects.

sanskrit: buddher uttarakālaṃ ca vedanā dṛśyate budhaiḥ eṣa vai rājaśārdūla vidhiḥ kṣetrajñabhāvanaḥ
english: After the intellect acts, sensation is seen by the wise; this indeed, O tiger among kings, is the process pertaining to the knower of the field.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca manasaś cāpi buddheś ca brūhi me lakṣaṇaṃ param etad adhyātmaviduṣāṃ paraṃ kāryaṃ vidhīyate
english: Yudhishthira said: Tell me the supreme distinguishing mark of both mind and intellect — this is considered the highest task of those who know the inner self.

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca buddhir ātmānugā tāta utpātena vidhīyate tadāśritā hi saṃjñaiṣā vidhis tasyaiṣaṇe bhavet
english: The serpent said: Intellect follows the self, dear one — it is established through its arising; for the very cognition that depends on it is its regulation in its seeking.

sanskrit: buddher guṇavidhir nāsti manas tu guṇavad bhavet buddhir utpadyate kārye manas tūtpannam eva hi
english: There is no rule of qualities for intellect; but the mind may be qualified. Intellect arises in regard to action, whereas the mind is simply something that arises.

sanskrit: etad viśeṣaṇaṃ tāta manobuddhyor mayeritam tvam apy atrābhisaṃbuddhaḥ kathaṃ vā manyate bhavān
english: This distinction between mind and intellect has been stated by me, dear one. You too are wise in this matter — or what does your lordship think?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca aho buddhimatāṃ śreṣṭha śubhā buddhir iyaṃ tava viditaṃ veditavyaṃ te kasmān mām anupṛcchasi
english: Yudhishthira said: Ah, O best among the wise, auspicious is your intellect! What is to be known is known by you — why do you ask me?

sanskrit: sarvajñaṃ tvāṃ kathaṃ moha āviśat svargavāsinam evam adbhutakarmāṇam iti me saṃśayo mahān
english: How did delusion enter you, an omniscient one, a dweller in heaven, one of such wondrous deeds? This is my great doubt.

sanskrit: sarpa uvāca suprajñam api cec chūram ṛddhir mohayate naram vartamānaḥ sukhe sarvo nāvaitīti matir mama
english: The serpent said: Prosperity deludes a man even if he is very wise and heroic; whoever is presently experiencing happiness does not fully know — this is my view.

sanskrit: so 'ham aiśvaryamohena madāviṣṭo yudhiṣṭhira patitaḥ pratisaṃbuddhas tvāṃ tu saṃbodhayāmy aham
english: I, O Yudhishthira, was deluded by the intoxication of sovereignty, overcome by pride, and fell; now awakened, I awaken you in turn.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ mahārāja tvayā mama paraṃtapa kṣīṇaḥ śāpaḥ sukṛcchro me tvayā saṃbhāṣya sādhunā
english: Your task on my behalf has been accomplished, O great king, O scorcher of foes; my curse, hard to bear, has been exhausted by your conversing with me thus virtuously.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi divi divyena vimānena caran purā abhimānena mattaḥ san kaṃ cin nānyam acintayam
english: For I was formerly traveling in heaven in a divine chariot, intoxicated with pride, and thought of no one else as my equal.

sanskrit: brahmarṣidevagandharvayakṣarākṣasakiṃnarāḥ karān mama prayacchanti sarve trailokyavāsinaḥ
english: Brahmin-seers, gods, gandharvas, yakshas, rakshasas, and kinnaras — all the inhabitants of the three worlds paid tribute to me.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣā yaṃ prapaśyāmi prāṇinaṃ pṛthivīpate tasya tejo harāmy āśu tad dhi dṛṣṭibalaṃ mama
english: Whichever living being I would look upon with my eye, O lord of the earth, its radiance I would swiftly steal away — for that was the power of my gaze.

sanskrit: brahmarṣīṇāṃ sahasraṃ hi uvāha śibikāṃ mama sa mām apanayo rājan bhraṃśayām āsa vai śriyaḥ
english: Indeed a thousand brahmin seers would bear my palanquin. That arrogance, O king, caused me to fall from my glory.

sanskrit: tatra hy agastyaḥ pādena vahan spṛṣṭo mayā muniḥ adṛṣṭena tato 'smy ukto dhvaṃsa sarpeti vai ruṣā
english: For there the sage Agastya, while bearing me, was touched by my foot; then, unseen, he spoke to me in anger: 'Fall, become a serpent!'

sanskrit: tatas tasmād vimānāgrāt pracyutaś cyutabhūṣaṇaḥ prapatan bubudhe ''tmānaṃ vyālībhūtam adhomukham
english: Then, fallen from the top of that chariot, stripped of my ornaments, as I was tumbling down I became aware of myself transformed into a serpent, falling headlong.

sanskrit: ayācaṃ tam ahaṃ vipraṃ śāpasyānto bhaved iti ajñānāt saṃpravṛttasya bhagavan kṣantum arhasi
english: I besought that brahmin, 'Let there be an end to the curse' — saying 'O blessed one, you should forgive one who acted out of ignorance.'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa mām uvācedaṃ prapatantaṃ kṛpānvitaḥ yudhiṣṭhiro dharmarājaḥ śāpāt tvāṃ mokṣayiṣyati
english: Then, filled with compassion, he spoke to me as I was falling: 'Yudhishthira, the dharma-king, will release you from the curse.'

sanskrit: abhimānasya ghorasya balasya ca narādhipa phale kṣīṇe mahārāja phalaṃ puṇyam avāpsyasi
english: 'When the fruit of your terrible pride and power has been exhausted, O lord of men, O great king, you will attain the fruit of your merit.'

sanskrit: tato me vismayo jātas tad dṛṣṭvā tapaso balam brahma ca brāhmaṇatvaṃ ca yena tvāham acūcudam
english: Then wonder arose in me, seeing the power of asceticism, and of Brahman, and of brahminhood — by which you, Yudhishthira, have enlightened me.

sanskrit: satyaṃ damas tapo yogam ahiṃsā dānanityatā sādhakāni sadā puṃsāṃ na jātir na kulaṃ nṛpa
english: Truth, self-restraint, asceticism, yoga, non-injury, and constancy in giving — these are ever the instruments of accomplishment for human beings; not birth, not lineage, O king.

sanskrit: ariṣṭa eṣa te bhrātā bhīmo mukto mahābhujaḥ svasti te 'stu mahārāja gamiṣyāmi divaṃ punaḥ
english: This brother of yours, Bhima of mighty arms, is unharmed and freed. May it be well with you, O great king — I shall go to heaven again.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvājagaraṃ dehaṃ tyaktvā sa nahuṣo nṛpaḥ divyaṃ vapuḥ samāsthāya gatas tridivam eva ha
english: Vaishampayana said: Having spoken thus and abandoned the python's body, that king Nahusha assumed his divine form and departed to the third heaven.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro 'pi dharmātmā bhrātrā bhīmena saṃgataḥ dhaumyena sahitaḥ śrīmān āśramaṃ punar abhyagāt
english: The virtuous Yudhishthira too, reunited with his brother Bhima, accompanied by Dhaumya, glorious as he was, returned to the hermitage.

sanskrit: tato dvijebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ sametebhyo yathātatham kathayām āsa tat sarvaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then Yudhishthira the dharma-king related all of that exactly as it had happened to all the assembled twice-born.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā te dvijāḥ sarve bhrātaraś cāsya te trayaḥ āsan suvrīḍitā rājan draupadī ca yaśasvinī
english: Having heard that, all those twice-born, his three brothers, and the illustrious Draupadi were greatly ashamed, O king.

sanskrit: te tu sarve dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ hitepsayā maivam ity abruvan bhīmaṃ garhayanto 'sya sāhasam
english: All those foremost twice-born, wishing well for the Pandavas, said to Bhima 'Do not do so again,' reproving his recklessness.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu bhayān muktaṃ prekṣya bhīmaṃ mahābalam harṣam āhārayāṃ cakrur vijahruś ca mudā yutāḥ
english: But the Pandavas, seeing the mighty Bhima freed from danger, rejoiced and sported together filled with delight.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca nidāghāntakaraḥ kālaḥ sarvabhūtasukhāvahaḥ tatraiva vasatāṃ teṣāṃ prāvṛṭ samabhipadyata
english: Vaishampayana said: While they were dwelling there, the rainy season arrived — that time which ends the hot season and brings comfort to all beings.

sanskrit: chādayanto mahāghoṣāḥ khaṃ diśaś ca balāhakāḥ pravavarṣur divārātram asitāḥ satataṃ tadā
english: Great roaring dark clouds, covering the sky and all directions, poured rain continuously day and night at that time.

sanskrit: tapātyayaniketāś ca śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ apetārkaprabhājālāḥ savidyudvimalaprabhāḥ
english: Hundreds and thousands of clouds, heralding the end of the hot season, their nets of solar radiance departed, gleaming brightly with lightning.

sanskrit: virūḍhaśaṣpā pṛthivī mattadaṃśasarīsṛpā babhūva payasā siktā śāntadhūmarajo 'ruṇā
english: The earth, with fresh young grass growing, filled with intoxicated gadflies and crawling creatures, drenched with water, its dust and smoke settled, glowed reddish.

sanskrit: na sma prajñāyate kiṃ cid ambhasā samavastṛte samaṃ vā viṣamaṃ vāpi nadyo vā sthāvarāṇi vā
english: Nothing could be discerned through the water that covered everything equally — neither level ground nor uneven, neither rivers nor stationary objects.

sanskrit: kṣubdhatoyā mahāghoṣāḥ śvasamānā ivāśugāḥ sindhavaḥ śobhayāṃ cakruḥ kānanāni tapātyaye
english: Rivers with their waters churned up, making great noise, flowing swiftly as if breathing hard, adorned the forests at the end of the hot season.

sanskrit: nadatāṃ kānanānteṣu śrūyante vividhāḥ svanāḥ vṛṣṭibhis tāḍyamānānāṃ varāhamṛgapakṣiṇām
english: In the depths of the forests, various sounds were heard of boars, deer, and birds being struck by the rain showers.

sanskrit: stokakāḥ śikhinaś caiva puṃskokilagaṇaiḥ saha mattāḥ paripatanti sma dardurāś caiva darpitāḥ
english: Wagtails and peacocks, together with groups of male cuckoos, flew about in delight, and frogs too gamboled proudly.

sanskrit: tathā bahuvidhākārā prāvṛṇ meghānunāditā abhyatītā śivā teṣāṃ caratāṃ marudhanvasu
english: Thus the rainy season, of many diverse forms, resounding with clouds, passed auspiciously for them as they roamed through the forests and deserts.

sanskrit: krauñcahaṃsagaṇākīrṇā śarat praṇihitābhavat rūḍhakakṣavanaprasthā prasannajalanimnagā
english: Autumn arrived, filled with flocks of cranes and geese, with grown-over thickets, forests, and plains, with rivers running clear.

sanskrit: vimalākāśanakṣatrā śarat teṣāṃ śivābhavat mṛgadvijasamākīrṇā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām
english: With its pure sky and stars, autumn proved auspicious for those great-souled Pandavas, filled with deer and birds.

sanskrit: paśyantaḥ śāntarajasaḥ kṣapā jaladaśītalāḥ grahanakṣatrasaṃghaiś ca somena ca virājitāḥ
english: They beheld the nights, dust-free and cool with rain-water, brilliant with groups of planets and stars, and radiant with the moon.

sanskrit: kumudaiḥ puṇḍarīkaiś ca śītavāridharāḥ śivāḥ nadīḥ puṣkariṇīś caiva dadṛśuḥ samalaṃkṛtāḥ
english: They saw rivers and pools beautifully adorned with night-blooming lotuses and white lotuses, their waters cool, auspicious and bearing cool water.

sanskrit: ākāśanīkāśataṭāṃ nīpanīvārasaṃkulām babhūva caratāṃ harṣaḥ puṇyatīrthāṃ sarasvatīm
english: Joy arose for them as they roamed, seeing the Sarasvati river with its banks resembling the sky, crowded with kadamba and wild rice, full of holy fords.

sanskrit: te vai mumudire vīrāḥ prasannasalilāṃ śivām paśyanto dṛḍhadhanvānaḥ paripūrṇāṃ sarasvatīm
english: Those heroes, those firm bowmen, rejoiced indeed, beholding the Sarasvati with its clear, auspicious, brimming waters.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ puṇyatamā rātriḥ parvasaṃdhau sma śāradī tatraiva vasatām āsīt kārttikī janamejaya
english: For them dwelling there, the most auspicious night was that autumnal Kartika night at the conjunction of the lunar fortnight, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: puṇyakṛdbhir mahāsattvais tāpasaiḥ saha pāṇḍavāḥ tat sarvaṃ bharataśreṣṭhāḥ samūhur yogam uttamam
english: Together with ascetics of great souls who had performed meritorious deeds, the Pandavas, best of the Bharatas, assembled there and practised the highest yoga.

sanskrit: tamisrābhyudaye tasmin dhaumyena saha pāṇḍavāḥ sūtaiḥ paurogavaiś caiva kāmyakaṃ prayayur vanam
english: At the rising of the darkness of that night, the Pandavas together with Dhaumya, with their charioteers and cooks, departed for the Kamyaka forest.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kāmyakaṃ prāpya kaunteyā yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ kṛtātithyā munigaṇair niṣeduḥ saha kṛṣṇayā
english: Vaishampayana said: Having reached Kamyaka, the sons of Kunti with Yudhishthira at their head, duly honored as guests by the groups of sages, took their seats together with Krishna (Draupadi).

sanskrit: tatas tān pariviśvastān vasataḥ pāṇḍunandanān brāhmaṇā bahavas tatra samantāt paryavārayan
english: Then many brahmins surrounded from all sides those sons of Pandu as they dwelt there in full confidence.
